concerns.text: The mixed‑effects regression treats each sliding‑window FTLE estimate as an independent observation with only a random intercept per trajectory. Because windows overlap within a single trajectory, their errors are serially correlated beyond what a random intercept captures. Applying a Durbin‑Watson test on the FTLE time‑series and then using Newey‑West HAC correction on the regression residuals does not fully address the hierarchical autocorrelation structure. A more appropriate model would include a random slope for window size or explicitly model the within‑trajectory correlation (e.g., using a covariance structure for repeated measures).

The baseline for each window size is computed with Rosenstein’s algorithm on the clean trajectory, while noisy FTLEs are computed with a QR‑based method. Although the algorithms differ, the baseline values are deterministic functions of the same underlying system and are used as fixed offsets (Δλ). This makes the dependent variable (Δλ) partially a deterministic transformation of the predictor ‘window size’ (T) rather than a purely stochastic outcome, which can inflate apparent significance of the 1/T term. The analysis should treat the baseline uncertainty (e.g., via its convergence error) as part of the error model rather than assuming it is exact.
